outcomes: Load a CT series while preserving intensity, origin, spacing, direction, and series identity.
Convert candidate locations between world coordinates and array indices and verify the transform with round-trip tests.
Build candidate-centered tensors through a custom Dataset and DataLoader with documented shape and label contracts.
Validate samples visually and programmatically, then tune loading performance without changing sample meaning.

sections.title: Treat a CT volume as pixels plus geometry
sections.summary: The NumPy array alone cannot locate a candidate expressed in physical coordinates.
body: A CT reader supplies an intensity array and metadata describing where each voxel lies in patient or scanner space. Preserve origin, voxel spacing, direction, and the series UID together. Array axes are commonly ordered differently from physical x, y, z coordinates, so conversions must state both conventions.

CT values may be clipped or windowed for the learning problem, but retain the original dtype and range long enough to inspect them. Normalization is part of the input contract: write the clipping limits, scaling rule, output dtype, and whether air or padding receives a special value.
points: Series UID identifies the source scan.
Origin locates an index-space reference point in world coordinates.
Spacing gives physical distance between neighboring voxels.
Direction records axis orientation and must not be silently assumed identity.

callouts.title: Array order is not world order
callouts.body: Many arrays use index order [z, y, x] while annotations use physical [x, y, z]. Name coordinate components instead of relying on positional intuition.

sections.title: Make coordinate conversion an independently tested function
sections.summary: Candidate crops are only useful when their physical centers map to the intended voxels.
body: World-to-index conversion subtracts the origin, applies inverse direction, divides by spacing, and then reorders axes for the array. Rounding policy matters: a continuous center can fall between voxels, while slicing requires integer indices. Keep the floating index available for diagnostics before selecting a crop center.

Test known points and round trips in both directions. A round trip should recover the original world location within an absolute tolerance stated in millimeters and justified from the transform precision and voxel spacing. Also test negative indices, upper boundaries, anisotropic spacing, and non-identity direction where the source format provides it.

code.title: Test rather than trust a conversion

sections.title: Crop candidates with explicit boundary behavior
sections.summary: A fixed-size tensor simplifies batching only when edge cases follow a documented padding rule.
body: Convert the candidate center to array coordinates, compute half-widths for depth, height, and width, and slice a fixed physical or voxel extent. Candidates near a boundary require clipping plus padding. Do not allow Python negative slices to wrap around to the opposite side of the volume.

Return the crop, label, series UID, center, and any metadata needed for later error analysis. Assert the final crop shape for every item. If crops are defined in voxels, note that physical coverage changes with spacing; if defined in millimeters, resampling becomes part of the contract.

code.title: Validate every returned sample

callouts.title: Keep provenance in the batch
callouts.body: Identifiers and centers do not enter the network, but they are essential when a false positive must be traced back to the source volume.

sections.title: Separate indexing from loading and transformation
sections.summary: A map-style Dataset should make one index resolve to one reproducible sample contract.
body: Build an immutable candidate list during initialization and keep expensive volume decoding lazy. __len__ reports the candidate count; __getitem__ resolves one candidate, loads or retrieves its volume, crops it, normalizes it, and returns tensors plus metadata. Repeated logic belongs in ordinary functions that can be tested without a DataLoader worker.

Decide whether a cache stores decoded source volumes or derived crops. A process-local read-through cache is often simpler than sharing mutable state across workers. Include source and preprocessing versions in persistent cache keys so stale arrays cannot be mistaken for current data.

code.title: A typed sample boundary

sections.title: Tune DataLoader only after sample correctness
sections.summary: Workers, prefetching, pinned memory, and persistent processes change throughput and lifecycle, not dataset semantics.
body: Start with num_workers=0 because errors have direct tracebacks and all state lives in one process. Once samples are correct, measure additional workers, CUDA pinned memory, prefetch_factor, and persistent_workers. More workers can slow storage-bound or cache-heavy workloads. Pair pin_memory=True with non_blocking=True when moving a batch to CUDA, and measure whether transfer is actually the bottleneck.

For reproducible random behavior, seed PyTorch, Python, and NumPy code used inside each worker and pass a seeded torch.Generator to DataLoader. On Windows and macOS, keep worker functions at module scope and create or iterate a multi-worker loader only below an if __name__ == '__main__' guard. In an interactive notebook, use num_workers=0 until Dataset and worker code lives in an importable module. Do not expect exact results to remain identical across PyTorch releases or different platforms.

code.title: Seed worker-local libraries
code.source:
import random
import numpy as np
import torch
from torch.utils import data

def seed_worker(worker_id):
    worker_seed = torch.initial_seed() % 2**32
    random.seed(worker_seed)
    np.random.seed(worker_seed)

def make_loader(dataset, *, seed=17, num_workers=0):
    """Build a loader; call under a main guard when workers > 0."""
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    return data.DataLoader(
        dataset,
        batch_size=8,
        shuffle=True,
        num_workers=num_workers,
        worker_init_fn=seed_worker,
        generator=generator,
        pin_memory=torch.cuda.is_available(),
        persistent_workers=num_workers > 0,
    )

sections.title: Inspect data in physical and tensor context
sections.summary: Plots catch coordinate, orientation, clipping, and label errors that aggregate statistics cannot localize.
body: Display orthogonal slices through positive and negative candidates, mark the intended center, and include series identity and intensity range in the caption. Sample large, small, central, boundary, and unusual examples rather than only attractive positives.

Pair visual review with automated summaries: class counts, missing series, crop extrema, non-finite values, duplicated identities, and per-split prevalence. Save the report with the split and preprocessing revision so later model changes can be separated from data changes.
points: Review raw and normalized views side by side.
Confirm left/right and superior/inferior orientation where relevant.
Plot candidate center in more than one plane.
Trace every suspicious crop back to its source metadata.
